criteria.rationale: Examined R1-R3, D1, HookMain and runHookRunner. Verified that root resolution is unchanged and delegation supplies the hook name and project working directory. Actual root bindings and non-recursive dispatch remain responsibilities of the instance-owned runner; the fixture does not establish those properties for a real instance. No new authority is inferred from the policy.
The new execution path waits synchronously for one runner and introduces no shared mutable state or background goroutines. No separate cancellation interface is introduced.

Reviewed invocation-name dispatch through cmd/pose/main.go, HookMain, runner execution and status reporting. Independently ran the three targeted tests and the broader hook test selection successfully.

Policy errors identify the policy and offending runner or schema; launch errors identify the hook runner. Runner output is forwarded and managed-hook status identifies the delegated executable or refusal reason.

Examined the old and new HookMain branches. An absent policy reaches the same pre-commit check and post-merge index commands. The new policy is opt-in; no CLI verb or MCP tool was removed or migrated.

D1 chooses an instance-owned runner because reading roots from instance configuration would alter who grants write authority. HookMain delegates before the default commands, while existing root-resolution code remains unchanged. This addresses the missing-bound-roots cause without adding root-discovery authority. The brief supplies no individual structural fact IDs requiring mappings.

Compared the changed hooks paragraphs in both locales and both scaffold copies. They consistently describe the optional policy, relative executable, hook-name argument, exit-code propagation and status output.

Reviewed policy refusal messages, executable validation, launch errors and managed-hook status. Reported failures provide the configuration path and actionable cause; runner failures preserve their output and exit status.

Compared the supplied range with the spec artifact declarations. Runtime changes are limited to hook delegation and status, with associated tests, launch-scan registration, validation-matrix registration and documentation. No unrelated refactor or root-authority change was introduced.

A single optional runner path and direct argv execution are a small sufficient alternative to teaching the engine instance-specific root discovery. The implementation adds no adapter registry, shell interpolation or speculative provider abstraction. This choice would need reconsideration if the engine were required to establish the runner's root bindings itself rather than trust an instance-owned executable.

findings.action: The strict hooks-policy reader decodes one JSON value without requiring EOF. For an existing executable runner, a policy containing {"schema_version":1,"runner":"scripts/hook.sh"} followed by garbage or another JSON object is accepted and executes the runner. This violates the strict-policy contract and fails open on malformed configuration. Require EOF after the object and cover trailing garbage and concatenated objects with tests asserting hook failure and no runner execution. The current invalid-policy tests do not exercise these inputs.
